title: Report fraud
summary: This page provides information on how to report suspected fraudulent business activity to the NSW Government.
intro:
Fraud is dishonestly obtaining a benefit by deception or other means.

If you suspect a business is defrauding the NSW Government in relation to any disaster payments, grants, voucher schemes, landowners and tenants relief, and/or any other NSW Government emergency assistance, you can report it online via the NSW Fraud Reporting Portal.

The types of fraud can include, but are not limited to:
who_can_apply: Anyone who is aware of, or suspects fraudulent business activity
what_you_need: the amount of money involved (if known)
evidence to validate your allegation (if available)
how and where it occurred (if applicable)
your contact details (you can remain anonymous if you prefer)

how_to_steps.text: Follow the prompts to report fraud.
A page confirming that your report has been received will display. Make a note of the confirmation number.

more_info.text: All reports of suspected fraud are taken seriously.
Service NSW has processes in place to ensure that any payments made on the basis of incorrect, incomplete, or fraudulent information are recovered.
If evidence of criminal activity is identified, the matter will be referred to NSW Police and law enforcement action may be taken.
If you have further information to add to your initial report, please call 13 77 88.

faqs.a: Anyone who is aware of, or suspects fraudulent business activity should report it.

faqs.q: How can I report fraud if I cannot report online?
faqs.a: Call 13 77 88 for advice on how to make your report.

faqs.q: What information do I need to report fraud?
faqs.a: You should have the name of the business, the type of fraud, the amount of money involved (if known), a summary of the allegation, evidence, how and where it occurred, and your contact details.
